s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence and absence of hair growth
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
Lesions range from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
key_facts: 2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions are asymptomatic
Lesions are round, hypopigmented macules
Lesions are symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions have gradually coalesced
No hair growth at the site of the lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Stroma is formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis is observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Nevus sebaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells, consistent with nevus sebaceus

shortlist.label: Syringoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation and fibrous connective tissue stroma, similar to syringoma

shortlist.label: Trichoepithelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic hypopigmented macules with absence of hair growth, consistent with trichoepithelioma

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck, consistent with idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Hypopigmented macules with gradual coalescence, consistent with nevus depigmentosus

raw.rationale: The presence of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis in the dermis surrounding the tumor, along with the absence of hair growth in the affected areas, are characteristic features of Nevus sebaceus.

rejected.label: Syringoma
rejected.why: Syringoma typically presents with multiple small, skin-colored or yellowish papules, not hypopigmented macules.

rejected.label: Trichoepithelioma
rejected.why: Trichoepithelioma is a type of skin tumor that arises from hair follicles, but the absence of hair growth in the affected areas and the specific histopathologic findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
rejected.why: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis typically presents with multiple small, discrete, hypopigmented macules, but the histopathologic findings and the presence of a subepidermal tumor are not characteristic of this condition.

rejected.label: Nevus depigmentosus
rejected.why: Nevus depigmentosus is a congenital hypopigmented lesion that typically presents at birth or early childhood, and the histopathologic findings do not support this diagnosis.
